name: m2_baseline
description: Reproducible synthetic benchmark for the M2 episodic core (PRD §14.3). Each scenario seeds a fresh store with a small number of observations, then exercises recall and entity-timeline expectations covering anchor coupling, anchor propagation through a shared entity, and forward-falling open question resolution.

scenarios.name: decision_recall_with_evidence
scenarios.description: A single high-importance decision should be recalled by lexical query, with evidence linked back to the originating observation.

observations.content: User decided to implement MCP memory with Python, SQLite FTS5, and LanceDB.

scenarios.name: anchor_coupling_within_observation
scenarios.description: When an observation explicitly mentions both a person and a date+venue, the event should be coupled to both anchors and the person should inherit them via entity_anchors.

observations.content: Remember important: Carter Stewart presented at Metropolitan Museum on 2026-09-22.

scenarios.name: anchor_propagation_through_shared_entity
scenarios.description: Anchors attached to one observation must propagate to a later observation that shares an entity but does not restate the anchor.

observations.content: Remember important: The MCP workshop happened on 2026-09-22 at Metropolitan Museum.
Remember important: Carter Stewart presented the MCP workshop.

scenarios.name: forward_falling_open_question_resolution
scenarios.description: An early observation creates an open 'when' question for a presenter; a later observation that supplies the date+venue should mark the question answered with the new anchor evidence.

observations.content: Remember important: Carter Stewart presented the statistics workshop.
Remember important: Carter Stewart presented at Metropolitan Museum on 2026-09-22.

scenarios.name: preference_recall_across_decision_and_preference_events
scenarios.description: Two related observations should produce two events; recall by topic should surface both with non-zero importance.

observations.content: User decided to use Python for the long-term memory MCP server.
User prefers SQLite + LanceDB local-first storage for the memory project.

scenarios.name: segment_heat_and_narrative_cache
scenarios.description: Repeated mentions of the same primary entity should join the same MemorySegment and produce a non-trivial segment heat. The recall path should attach a query-specific entity narrative.

observations.content: Remember important: Carter Stewart presented the M3 lifecycle workshop at Metropolitan Museum on 2026-09-22.
Remember important: Carter Stewart explained MemoryOS heat and PersistentMemory promotion.
Remember important: Carter Stewart followed up with a Q&A on entity narratives.

scenarios.name: forget_event_cascade
scenarios.description: Forgetting one supporting event should stale entity narratives, reduce the supporting persistent memory reinforcement count, and hide the forgotten event from default search.

observations.content: User decided important: SQLite remains canonical for the long-term memory server.
User decided important: LanceDB remains a rebuildable retrieval index.

supporting_event_summary_substrings: LanceDB remains a rebuildable retrieval index
